correctness.rationale: In a multipartite graph the future of a given initial phase class depends only on whether external parts possess blinking 1, so each part reduces to its nonempty initial support in seven masks; duplicate support types saturate at multiplicity two because each part excludes itself in detecting a blinking neighbor. Every possible graph with r>=3 therefore corresponds to one of precisely 2158 realizable 7-tuples with counts 0,1,2. Reimplemented exact tagged transition on all 2158: obtained 2009 preperiod-2 synchronized cases, 65 preperiod-5, 43 preperiod-6, two period-four recurrent support types, one asynchronous period-three recurrent support type, and all other claimed classes, no nonperiodic asynchronous basin, period dividing 12. The reduction, not bounded small-graph tests, proves the unrestricted family. Exact inclusion–exclusion counts U2=2^n−2 and U3=3^n−3*2^n+3 yield all stated labelled orbit counts; F^18=F^6 follows from preperiod <=6 and lcm(3,4)=12. Witness configurations attain t=3 all singleton and t=6 when any non-singleton part.

final_claim: For every labelled complete multipartite graph with at least three nonempty parts under synchronous 3-color inhibitory firefly updates, every trajectory reaches its eventual 3- or 4-cycle by update six; all nonsynchronous periodic orbits have zero preperiod; their exact counts are sum_i U3(n_i)/3 and sum_{i<j}U2(n_i)U2(n_j)/2, and F^18=F^6 with sharp 3 vs 6 first-entry cutoffs.
limitations: r>=3 simple labelled complete multipartite graphs, exact three-color synchronous inhibitory update only.
No claim about arbitrary graphs, stochastic inhibition, or other phase counts.
